\chapter{Hacer y parecer}
\label{ch:es-hacer-y-parecer}
\hlchaptermodality{511}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say that something seems a certain way, is kept up, is about a topic, is carried out or usually happens.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 511: I can say that something seems a certain way, is kept up, is about a topic, is carried out or usually happens.

\section[parecer]{parecer — to seem}

\label{lesson:ES-C511-parecer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to hate, then the Spanish for to surprise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: parecer}
\textbf{parecer} — \textquotedblleft{}to seem\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Parece fácil, pero no lo es.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It seems easy, but it is not.}
\end{quote}

\emph{¿Qué te parece?} — what do you think? It takes a \emph{z} in \emph{parezco}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parecer}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parecer}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{parecer}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to hate, then the Spanish for to surprise, then say \emph{parecer} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does parecer mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To seem\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[tratar]{tratar — to treat; to be about}

\label{lesson:ES-C511-tratar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to seem, then the Spanish for to keep.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: tratar}
\textbf{tratar} — \textquotedblleft{}to treat; to be about\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The film is about a family.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Tratar de} + infinitive — to try to.

\section[realizar]{realizar — to carry out, to do}

\label{lesson:ES-C511-realizar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to keep, then the Spanish for to treat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: realizar}
\textbf{realizar} — \textquotedblleft{}to carry out, to do\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Realizamos obras en la calle.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We are carrying out works on the street.}
\end{quote}

A false friend: to realise is \emph{darse cuenta}.

\section[soler]{soler — to usually do}

\label{lesson:ES-C511-soler}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to treat, then the Spanish for to carry out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: soler}
\textbf{soler} — \textquotedblleft{}to usually do\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Suelo cenar a las nueve.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I usually have dinner at nine.}
\end{quote}

Always followed by an infinitive. The o breaks into ue: \emph{suelo}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[(dialogue)]{Palabras de los capítulos 503-507 — a first pass}

\label{lesson:ES-R511-repaso-palabras-de-los-capitulos-503-507}



\begin{quote}
Say the Spanish for to carry out and to usually do.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item to lose weight, to put up with, the effort, the pressure, patient
  \item to recycle, pollution, to protect, the factory, to damage
  \item education, to attend, the explanation, to rehearse, success
  \item to give, to wrap, the toy, to congratulate, to hug
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To lose weight? (\textbf{adelgazar}.) To put up with? (\textbf{aguantar}.) The effort? (\textbf{el esfuerzo}.) The pressure? (\textbf{la presión}.) Patient? (\textbf{paciente}.) To recycle? (\textbf{reciclar}.) Pollution? (\textbf{la contaminación}.) To protect? (\textbf{proteger}.) The factory? (\textbf{la fábrica}.) To damage? (\textbf{dañar}.) Education? (\textbf{la educación}.) To attend? (\textbf{asistir}.) The explanation? (\textbf{la explicación}.) To rehearse? (\textbf{ensayar}.) Success? (\textbf{el éxito}.) To give? (\textbf{regalar}.) To wrap? (\textbf{envolver}.) The toy? (\textbf{el juguete}.) To congratulate? (\textbf{felicitar}.) To hug? (\textbf{abrazar}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Palabras de los capítulos 508-511 — a second pass}

\label{lesson:ES-R511-repaso-palabras-de-los-capitulos-508-511}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item to plan, to wish, the goal, hope, the agreement
  \item to apologise, to trust, to fight, to hate, to surprise

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To vote? (\textbf{votar}.) The tax? (\textbf{el impuesto}.) The population? (\textbf{la población}.) The inhabitant? (\textbf{el habitante}.) The debate? (\textbf{el debate}.) Incredible? (\textbf{increíble}.) Independent? (\textbf{independiente}.) Well known? (\textbf{conocido}.) Current? (\textbf{actual}.) Acceptable? (\textbf{aceptable}.) To plan? (\textbf{planear}.) To wish? (\textbf{desear}.) The goal? (\textbf{la meta}.) Hope? (\textbf{la esperanza}.) The agreement? (\textbf{el acuerdo}.) To apologise? (\textbf{disculparse}.) To trust? (\textbf{fiarse}.) To fight? (\textbf{pelear}.) To hate? (\textbf{odiar}.) To surprise? (\textbf{sorprender}.) To seem? (\textbf{parecer}.) To keep? (\textbf{mantener}.) To treat? (\textbf{tratar}.) To carry out? (\textbf{realizar}.) To usually do? (\textbf{soler}.)
